title: CHAPTER 7: AGRICULTURAL ECONOMICS AND RURAL FINANCE

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Land Reforms in India focus on institutional changes in agrarian structure to promote equitable ownership and productivity.
Agricultural credit is vital for farm inputs and categorized into institutional (Banks, RRBs, Cooperatives) and non-institutional sources.
The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facilitates timely, hassle-free credit to farmers for crop production and working capital.
Agricultural Marketing involves processes ranging from harvesting, grading, storage, and transport to final sale.
NABARD operates as the apex financial institution providing refi­nance and guidance for rural and agricultural growth.

cells: Security of tenure; regulate rent; right to purchase land
Set maximum land holding limits; redistribute surplus land
Successful in Punjab, Haryana; poor progress in east India
~4 million acres donated; most land unfit for cultivation

blocks.content: Agricultural credit is the financial backbone of farming. It enables farmers to purchase inputs, equipment, and meet consumption needs. Credit can be short-term (crop loans), medium-term (equipment purchase), or long-term (land development, irrigation).

items: Introduced in 1998-99; based on R.V. Gupta Committee recommendations
Provides revolving credit for crop production, post-harvest, maintenance, consumption
Interest subvention: 2% by Govt + 3% prompt repayment incentive = 4% effective rate
Limit based on land holding and crop type; enhanced to include allied activities in 2019
As of 2024: ~7.5 crore KCC holders; target to cover all PM-KISAN beneficiaries

blocks.content: Agricultural marketing includes all activities involved in the flow of agricultural products from farm to consumer. Efficient marketing reduces post-harvest losses, ensures remunerative prices to farmers, and stabilises consumer prices.

cells: State-regulated mandis; farmers must sell in designated mandis; APMC Act governs; controversial — many states amending
Floor price announced by Govt; based on C2+50% formula recommended by CACP; covers 23 crops
Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices; recommends MSP; under Ministry of Agriculture
FCI (Food Corporation of India), NAFED, State agencies; procure at MSP from farmers
Electronic National Agriculture Market; online trading platform; connects 1000+ mandis; price discovery
Farmer Producer Organisation/Company; collective marketing; aggregation reduces transaction cost
AGMARK certification; ensures quality standards; important for exports
Temperature-controlled supply chain; reduces post-harvest losses; NHB, NCCD promote
NCDEX, MCX; futures trading in agri commodities; price risk management (hedging)
Rythu Bazars (AP), Uzhavar Sandhi (TN); eliminates middlemen; better farmer prices

blocks.content: NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) was established on July 12, 1982 based on the recommendations of the Shivaraman Committee. It is the apex institution for agricultural and rural credit in India, headquartered in Mumbai.

items: NABARD's statutory role, establishment year, and refinance functions are frequently asked in competitive exams.
Distinguish between institutional credit (Cooperatives, RRBs, Commercial Banks) and non-institutional credit sources.
Key features and target beneficiaries of the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme are high-priority exam topics.
Refinancing commercial banks, RRBs, co-operative banks, MFIs for agriculture and rural development: Credit Functions
Capacity building, training, technology promotion, Agri Clinic and Agri Business Centres (ACABCs): Development Functions
Inspects and supervises RRBs and State Co-operative Banks (StCBs) and DCCBs: Regulatory Functions
World's largest microfinance programme; started 1992; links self-help groups to banks: SHG-Bank Linkage Programme
PSL shortfall funds deposited in RIDF; used for rural infrastructure by State Govts: RIDF (Rural Infrastructure Development Fund)
Direct credit to FPOs; no collateral if turnover < Rs.1 crore: NABKISAN
